recent_posts.title: Practical west tips for Zephyr workspace management
recent_posts.summary: A collection of practical tips for using the Zephyr `west` workspace manager more effectively. Topics covered include: installing specific SDK versions and toolchains with `west sdk install`, limiting clone depth via `clone-depth` in the manifest, restricting `west update` imports using `name-allowlist` and `path-prefix`, caching fetches with `update.auto-cache`, creating command aliases, writing custom west extension commands in Python, using `--narrow` and `--fetch-opt=--depth=1` to reduce network traffic, and pinning all dependencies to exact SHAs with `west manifest --resolve` for reproducible builds.

recent_posts.title: Why pragma pack(1) causes 7x overhead and how to fix it with packed aligned
recent_posts.summary: Using `#pragma pack(1)` on structs is common in embedded C for portable binary formats, but it forces the compiler to byte-decompose every field access — even perfectly aligned ones — resulting in up to 7x more instructions on RISC-V, ARM Cortex-M0, and Xtensa. The fix is combining `__attribute__((packed, aligned(4)))`: this preserves the no-padding layout while telling the compiler the struct base pointer is always aligned, enabling native single-instruction stores for aligned fields. The post also covers struct evolution risks (new fields silently landing at misaligned offsets), binary compatibility concerns with arrays of packed structs, and how to catch alignment regressions in CI using the `struct-lint` tool (DWARF-based) or `pahole`.

recent_posts.title: Connecting Matter-over-Thread Devices to the Internet
recent_posts.summary: Matter-over-Thread devices are designed to operate locally, with hubs handling internet communication. But when direct internet access is needed for telemetry or custom cloud services, Thread Border Routers can bridge the gap via NAT64. The post explains the networking stack (Thread, IPv6, NAT64, UDP), walks through a working UDP echo example on the nRF54LM20 DK using OpenThread's DNS client and UDP APIs, and covers practical constraints like payload size limits and the absence of TCP/TLS. For production use, CoAP over DTLS is recommended as a lightweight, encrypted protocol layer that runs over UDP.

recent_posts.title: Embedded Systems Roadmap: Bridging the Gap
recent_posts.summary: An embedded systems engineer shares the creation story of a comprehensive learning roadmap designed to bridge knowledge gaps between hardware and software disciplines. The roadmap addresses common challenges faced by engineers transitioning between fields, provides structured learning paths, and includes curated resources. The author discusses design decisions, community feedback, and offers practical guidance on using the roadmap effectively for career development in embedded systems.
